title: Install Homebrew on a new Mac (Apple Silicon or Intel)
summary: Homebrew is the most common package manager for macOS. The official install script installs it, and then you add it to your shell so the brew command works in Terminal.

aliases.text: how to install brew on macos

prerequisites: You know the login password of your Mac account (it must be an administrator account)
The Mac is connected to the internet

steps.explain: Check which kind of Mac you have. The output arm64 means Apple Silicon (M1 or newer). The output x86_64 means Intel. The next steps differ for the two.
steps.expect: One line: arm64 (Apple Silicon) or x86_64 (Intel).

steps.explain: Run the official Homebrew install script from brew.sh. Press Return when it asks, enter your Mac password when prompted, and wait. Do not add sudo in front of this command.
steps.expect: Lines starting with ==> are printed, and the output ends with 'Installation successful!'. The download takes several minutes.

steps.explain: Add Homebrew to your shell profile so that brew is found in every new Terminal window. On Apple Silicon use this line.
steps.expect: No output. One line is appended to ~/.zprofile. Running this command twice adds the line twice, which is harmless.

alternatives.explain: On Intel Macs use this line instead, because Homebrew is installed in /usr/local.
alternatives.expect: No output. One line is appended to ~/.zprofile.

steps.explain: Load Homebrew into the current Terminal window now, so you do not have to open a new window. On Apple Silicon use this line.

alternatives.explain: On Intel Macs use this line instead.

verify.expect: The first line starts with 'Homebrew ' followed by a version number.

rollback.explain: Remove the eval line that was added to ~/.zprofile. Open the file in TextEdit or any editor and delete the line that contains brew shellenv.
To remove Homebrew completely, run the official uninstall.sh script from the Homebrew/install repository on GitHub. Read the script first, because it deletes the Homebrew folders.

warnings: The install script asks for your Mac password and may install the Xcode Command Line Tools, which is a large download.
Never run the install script as root or with sudo in front of it. The script stops with the message: Don't run this as root!
Install Homebrew only from the official URL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh, which is linked from brew.sh.
